To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a simple, scalable, and low-cost method to produce large quantities of graphene flakes and that the resulting flakes can be used as a photoanode in a Schottky junction device with silicon.
we have successfully fabricated graphene/Si junctions and studied their electrical and photovoltaic properties.
the as-sonicated graphene product is a mixture of few-layer graphene, single-layer graphene and carbon nanoparticles, and the supernantant graphene has the best performance for the Schottky junction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fabrication of graphene/Schottky diodes and the study of their electrical properties.
the large-scale production and the electrical characterization of few-layer graphene devices on Si substrates.
the development of graphene-based Schottky diode devices and their applications in photovoltaic conversion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our results show the possibility to fabricate graphene/silicon junctions for photovoltaic applications, but the efficiency of such devices is not as high as expected, which is mainly due to the poor light harvesting capability of graphene.
the graphene/silicon junctions are promising for the development of future graphene-based photovoltaic devices.
the graphene/silicon diodes are promising candidates for photovoltaic applications, and the as-prepared graphene flakes can be applied in large-area electronic devices.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the graphene/Si Schottky junction devices are promising candidates for future optoelectronic applications.
the graphene/silicon heterojunctions are promising for photovoltaic applications.
the graphene flakes with different sizes and thicknesses can be produced in large scale and the supernatants are the best for device fabrication.
The main takeaway from our work is that
graphene can be used to produce Schottky photodetectors with high sensitivity and fast response time, and the graphene/silicon junctions are suitable for photovoltaic applications.
the large-scale production and device fabrication of few-layer graphene is feasible.
the large-area graphene/silicon junctions can be used as a platform for the development of graphene photovoltaic devices.
